title: Console launch triage: sampling-first traces and cost-summary fallback
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Summary: We need to reduce scope for the Console observability beta so we can ship a reliable, low-cost surface by the Q2 beta milestone. This ticket captures scope cuts, acceptance criteria, trade-offs, and rollout plan. Goal is to deliver a minimal but useful dashboard + tracing + cost summary that gives teams actionable insight while avoiding high-cardinality, expensive queries and heavy UI engineering.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard: 4 atomic metric tiles (route throughput, p95 latency, error-rate, token-cost estimation) are live and refresh within 60s
Tracing: Default tracing surface uses adaptive sampling (error-first + 1% background sampling) and exposes a single trace link from a tile to a lightweight trace viewer
Cost: Provide an aggregated cost summary card (7-day and 30-day totals) with daily trend line; full route-by-route cost breakdown deferred behind feature flag
Performance: Dashboard page load time < 1.5s median for logged-in users in NA region; queries must complete within 2s for primary tiles
Cost control: Query budget cap enforced for beta (soft limit) — telemetry must show >=30% lower query cost compared to the unrestricted prototype
Rollout: Feature flagged and can be enabled per-org in staging; canary rollout to 5% of beta users with rollback path documented
Docs: Minimal usage doc and troubleshooting guide published in Confluence with links to PRs and feature flags
decision_log: 2025-02-13 - Decided to prioritize sampling-first traces vs full-span capture to reduce ingestion and storage costs (decision: use error-priority + 1% background sampling).
2025-02-14 - Deferred per-route cost breakdown (detailed allocation) to reduce backend query complexity; will ship aggregate cost summary instead.
2025-02-18 - Agreed on 4 atomic dashboard tiles as reduction set (product + eng trade-off to keep iteration rapid).
2025-02-22 - Approved default trace viewer as lightweight link out (no deep trace UI in beta).
